free_tier.stated: Trial $0/mo, Dedicated IPv4 1, IPv6 /48 1, Machines 2, Runs for 7 days. The FAQ adds: 'It is free, there is no credit card and there is nobody to talk to: you fill in three fields and the address is yours. A real address out of the same /24 our paying customers are in, running for seven days.' The same page prices the paid plans: Solo $19/mo (1 IPv4, 1 /48, 2 machines), Team $49/mo (3 IPv4, 1 /48, 6 machines), Business $149/mo (8 IPv4, 1 /48, 20 machines, verification required).
free_tier.notes: Denominated in days, addresses and machines at once, so no single unit in the enum is honest: 7 days, 1 IPv4, 1 IPv6 /48, 2 machines. Nothing is counted in bytes or requests, because the vendor states it meters neither. The clock is the quota: the trial ends on day 7 and there is no renewal path, only a conversion to a paid plan that keeps the same address.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: The nearest equivalent is the lease size, and that is one dedicated IPv4 with one IPv6 /48 and 2 tunnels on the trial and on Solo. Size scales only by changing plan: Team is 3 IPv4 and 6 tunnels, Business 8 and 20.

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not an object
retention.notes: The address has a stated lifetime even though bytes do not. The trial runs 7 days. On a paid lease a missed renewal stops traffic but holds the address for another 7 days, and only then does it return to the pool, where it sits in quarantine for 30 days before reassignment. Paying inside the grace window restores the same address.

egress.terms: No allowance and no meter: 'We do not meter requests or bandwidth, so the plan decides how many addresses and machines you get and nothing decides how much you may send.' The same page prices the competition by the request and says an allowance is 'something to monitor, forecast and get paged about'.

interface_detail: The lease arrives as one WireGuard configuration file per tunnel, and that is the real access path; the schema's interface enum has no token for a tunnel. Ordering and management are a documented HTTP API at https://api.anchoredip.com/api/ covering plans, leases, tunnels, reverse DNS, renewal and payment, a dashboard that renders the same calls, and an MCP endpoint the pricing page names for agents. Two routing modes: 'source' writes Table = off and PostUp rules and needs wg-quick on Linux, while 'full' works in any WireGuard or AmneziaWG client.
tooling: wg-quick with the generated config in source mode, or any WireGuard or AmneziaWG client in full mode. The HTTP API creates a tunnel and returns the config once, and the vendor states the private key is not stored on its side, so it has to be written in the same step. The vendor states that a platform which cannot create a network interface, naming Heroku and Lambda, needs one small always-on machine to hold the tunnel; a Workers AI gateway is that shape, with the Worker making the calls and a VM carrying the tunnel.
chaining: Pairs with a free-tier VM: the VM holds the WireGuard tunnel and everything it sends leaves as the leased address, so a Workers AI gateway behind it presents one allowlistable identity to the partner API. The lease supplies the identity and the VM supplies the kernel interface the lease needs.

limits_note: Allocation and identity caps that name no kind in the vocabulary, kept rather than dropped: 2 tunnels on the trial and on Solo, 3 IPv4 and 6 tunnels on Team, 8 IPv4 and 20 tunnels on Business, one IPv4 per lease however many machines sit behind it, and 'One trial per billing email address, and one running at a time per network', with a second trial refused by a 400 that names the paid plans. Inbound is the narrower one: 'One machine per lease can also receive connections on that address.'
binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary fails at 45 GB a month and about 599,000 requests: the vendor states it does not meter requests or bandwidth, so there is no byte or request quota to reach, and the five-orders-an-hour throttle applies to lease management, not to traffic through the tunnel. The 7-day term is a property of the free offer rather than a limit traffic meets, and the ceiling that actually arrives first is the 2-tunnel allowance, which has no kind in the vocabulary.

identity_cost.detail: No card and no account are required for the trial: the pricing FAQ reads 'No card, and nobody to talk to', and POST /api/leases/ with plan trial returns an access_token and active status without payment. The billing email functions as the verification gate: the order body requires billing_email alongside organization_name and country, and the API documentation states 'A trial is one per billing email', with subsequent attempts refused. Paid plans accept credit card or bank transfer for invoices exceeding wire fees. Access is recovered by email through POST /api/auth/link/ and /api/auth/redeem/.

reliability_note: unverified: behind a sign-up. The source address one request through a lease returns cannot be measured without provisioning a lease: the keyless endpoints GET /api/plans/ and GET /api/ answered and returned only the plan catalogue and two links, with no per-request echo of the caller's address. Obtaining an address needs an order body with an organization name, country and billing email, and a WireGuard config that must be brought up on a machine holding the tunnel; no order or tunnel was created, so no exit address was observed and the rung is unchanged. Every address is screened against blocklists before assignment and re-checked daily afterwards.
confidence_note: Pricing, trial terms, unmetered bandwidth statements, order body structure, and routing modes are quoted from vendor documentation read on 2026-10-24. The registration class was measured using RIPE RDAP on 2026-10-24. Full measurement would require an active trial lease, tunnel throughput verification, and origin address resolution.

notes:
This record corrects dossier/egress/anchoredip.json, whose evidence entry reads 'space registered at RIPE NCC and announced from AS41800' with no registration class. That sentence invites the reading that AnchoredIP is an ISP holding a broadband allocation. RIPE RDAP read on 2026-10-24 returns 194.0.109.0/24 with country KZ, type ASSIGNED PA and registrant lir-kz-individual-1-MNT, an individual, and the autnum object for AS41800 sits under the same registrant. That is a personal provider-independent assignment in Kazakhstan, not an eyeball network, and the announced footprint is five IPv4 /24s plus one IPv6 /29, so every tenant sits inside 1,280 addresses. The vendor's own footer says the same thing: 'AnchoredIP - AS41800 - Karaganda, Kazakhstan'. The egress record must stop implying ISP registration; this record carries the measured class.

Each of three possible kinds of holder was tested for this space. (1) An ISP with a broadband allocation: refuted, because the RDAP type is ASSIGNED PA and the registrant is an individual maintenance object rather than a LIR member. (2) A hosting provider's block re-announced by AnchoredIP: refuted, because the AS registrant and the address registrant are the same person. (3) A resold block from a larger carrier: not refuted and not confirmed, because the parent 194.0.108.0-194.0.111.255 was not walked up to the LIR that allocated it. That walk was not run.

Two deviations are deliberate and both come from the evidence. First, identity_cost.kind is email and not anonymous. No card and no account is right, but POST /api/leases/ requires billing_email and the API page states 'A trial is one per billing email', so the email is the key the free offer is counted against; a reader planning several trials is misled by anonymous and not by email. Second, the registrant handle reads lir-kz-individual-1-MNT in the live RDAP response; the record carries the measured string.

Interface is recorded as rest and cli because the enum in scripts/dossier/schema.json has no token for wireguard, web-ui, api, socks5 or http-proxy, so the WireGuard path, the dashboard and the MCP endpoint are carried in interface_detail rather than dropped or forced into a token that would be wrong. The egress quote is on /vs/fixie and not on /pricing, which the egress record's source_url for that sentence points at.

What could not be settled: which /24 a leased address actually lands in. The vendor says the trial is 'a real address out of the same /24 our paying customers are in', and its own API example shows 194.0.108.99 while the RDAP sample is 194.0.109.0/24, so more than one /24 is in use and only a live lease would fix which. The latency figures are the vendor's measurements, not ours. And this rests on one sample: one /24 was classified out of the five announced, so the other four are unverified and the class claim is a claim about 194.0.109.0/24 rather than about the whole service.
